skill_drafts.name: Cache Miss Ratio Evaluation Protocol
skill_drafts.description: Standardized protocol for measuring and comparing cache eviction algorithm efficiency using miss ratio reduction relative to FIFO baseline. Handles wide-range trace datasets, byte-level footprint analysis, and outlier-resistant reporting across heterogeneous workloads.
skill_drafts.objective: Establish consistent, outlier-resistant cache performance benchmarking across heterogeneous workloads to enable fair algorithm comparison independent of trace-specific miss ratio ranges.
applicable_signals: Multiple heterogeneous cache workload traces available (block, key-value, object types)
Baseline FIFO algorithm performance data present
Object size variation in dataset requires byte-level footprint analysis
contraindications: Do not use for real-time production cache performance assessment under live traffic
Do not use to evaluate backend fill latency or throughput characteristics
Do not use to compare non-eviction cache properties (e.g., compression, serialization)
Do not use when trace data is insufficient or single-workload only
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Collect and prepare traces', 'detail': 'Gather traces spanning diverse cache workload types (block, key-value, object). Record object sizes for byte-level analysis if size variation is significant.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Establish FIFO baseline', 'detail': 'Run FIFO eviction algorithm on all traces and record miss ratio (MR_fifo) for each trace.'}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'Execute candidate algorithms', 'detail': 'Run each candidate eviction algorithm on all traces using same simulation environment. Record miss ratio (MR_algo) for each algorithm-trace pair.'}

{'step': 4, 'action': 'Calculate miss ratio reduction', 'detail': 'For each algorithm-trace pair: if MR_algo <= MR_fifo, compute (MR_fifo - MR_algo) / MR_fifo. If MR_algo > MR_fifo, compute -(MR_algo - MR_fifo) / MR_algo. Result is bounded [-1, 1].'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Compute summary statistics', 'detail': 'Calculate P10, P50, P90 percentiles and mean miss ratio reduction across all traces for each algorithm.'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Report byte-level metrics if needed', 'detail': 'If object size variation is significant, recalculate miss ratios using trace footprint in bytes instead of object count.'}

{'step': 7, 'action': 'Generate comparative report', 'detail': 'Present normalized miss ratio reduction scores, percentile summaries, and mean values for all algorithms. Highlight algorithms with consistent performance across percentiles.'}
triggers: Comparing two or more cache eviction algorithms across multiple traces
Need to normalize performance metrics across traces with widely varying miss ratio ranges
Evaluating algorithm efficiency as primary performance criterion
constraints: Require closed-loop trace replay simulation environment
Miss ratio reduction formula must bound results between -1 and 1 to prevent outlier inflation
Backend latency and throughput must be decoupled from eviction algorithm evaluation
Use pre-generated object values for on-demand cache fills to isolate algorithm impact
cautions: Wide trace miss ratio ranges can distort mean values; use percentile summaries (P10, P50, P90) alongside mean
Algorithms performing worse than FIFO on some traces will show negative reduction; report these transparently
Byte-level footprint analysis required only when object size distribution is non-uniform
output_contract: Normalized miss ratio reduction scores (bounded -1 to 1) for each algorithm-trace pair; percentile summaries (P10, P50, P90) and mean reduction values for each algorithm; optional byte-level miss ratio analysis; comparative ranking of algorithms by mean reduction and consistency across percentiles.

metadata.prompt: Execute a comparative cache eviction algorithm evaluation using normalized miss ratio reduction. (1) Collect traces spanning diverse cache workload types (block, key-value, object). (2) For each algorithm-trace pair, calculate miss ratio reduction as (MR_fifo - MR_algo) / MR_fifo, bounding results between -1 and 1 to prevent outlier distortion. (3) When an algorithm performs worse than FIFO, report negative reduction: -(MR_algo - MR_fifo) / MR_algo. (4) Compute percentile summaries (P10, P50, P90) and mean reduction across all traces. (5) Report byte-level miss ratios when object size variation is significant. (6) Isolate eviction algorithm impact by using simulation with pre-generated object values; do not conflate with backend fill latency or throughput.

skill_drafts.name: S3-FIFO Prototype Implementation in Cachelib
skill_drafts.description: Implement the S3-FIFO eviction algorithm in Cachelib by mapping S and M queues to linked lists and G to a hash table, working within slab memory management constraints and LRU-optimized architecture. Includes trace replay benchmarking setup to measure hit/miss performance against LRU, 2Q, and TinyLFU baselines.
skill_drafts.objective: Translate S3-FIFO algorithm design into production-ready cache library code with trace replay benchmarking
applicable_signals: Need to implement S3-FIFO in an existing cache library with slab memory management
Requirement to benchmark against LRU, 2Q, TinyLFU baselines
Access to production-grade cache library (Cachelib) with existing algorithm implementations
Availability of trace datasets for closed-loop replay evaluation
contraindications: Do not use when designing a new cache library architecture from scratch
Do not prioritize latency-critical path optimization before algorithm correctness is established
Do not attempt integration with non-slab memory managers without significant adaptation
Do not skip trace replay setup if comparative benchmarking is required
intervention_moves: Select linked list data structure for S and M queues to enable O(1) demotion and FIFO ordering
Select hash table for G queue to track ghost entries without excessive memory overhead
Integrate with Cachelib's slab allocator by pre-allocating memory during initialization
Adapt to Cachelib's metaprogramming patterns and compressed pointer optimizations
Build trace replay tool that cycles through traces in closed loop for benchmarking
Measure hit performance and on-demand fill cache misses with pre-generated object values
Calculate miss ratio reduction relative to FIFO baseline to isolate algorithm contribution
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Design data structure layout', 'detail': "Allocate linked list nodes for S and M queues; allocate hash table buckets for G queue; ensure compatibility with Cachelib's slab allocator"}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Implement queue operations', 'detail': 'Implement enqueue, dequeue, and demotion operations for S and M; implement lookup and insertion for G hash table'}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'Integrate with Cachelib framework', 'detail': "Adapt to Cachelib's memory management, metaprogramming patterns, and existing LRU-based optimizations; ensure no conflicts with compressed pointers or other optimizations"}

{'step': 4, 'action': 'Build trace replay tool', 'detail': 'Create closed-loop trace replay mechanism; support multiple trace formats (block, key-value, object); measure hit/miss counts and byte-level miss ratios'}

{'step': 5, 'action': 'Implement benchmarking harness', 'detail': 'Set up comparative evaluation against LRU, 2Q, and TinyLFU; calculate miss ratio reduction relative to FIFO baseline; collect performance metrics across cache sizes'}

{'step': 6, 'action': 'Validate and optimize', 'detail': 'Test on diverse trace datasets; measure hit performance and on-demand fill latency; verify that algorithm correctness is not compromised by Cachelib integration constraints'}
triggers: Implementing S3-FIFO in an existing cache library with slab memory management; need to benchmark against LRU, 2Q, TinyLFU baselines
constraints: Cachelib's slab memory management requires pre-allocation of all memory at initialization
Extensive use of metaprogramming and LRU-based optimizations (e.g., compressed pointers) tightly couples components
Linked list and hash table implementations must coexist with Cachelib's existing LRU-optimized infrastructure
Trace replay tool must support closed-loop replay for accurate miss ratio measurement
cautions: Cachelib developers have invested significant effort in throughput and scalability optimizations (lock combining, delayed promotion, try-lock-based promotion); ensure S3-FIFO implementation does not regress these gains
Ghost queue (G) memory overhead must be carefully managed to avoid negating efficiency gains
Benchmark results are sensitive to trace characteristics (block, key-value, object workloads); test across diverse trace types
output_contract: Deliverable is a working S3-FIFO implementation in Cachelib with: (1) functional S and M linked list queues and G hash table; (2) trace replay tool capable of closed-loop evaluation; (3) miss ratio metrics (request-based and byte-based) for S3-FIFO and three baseline algorithms; (4) comparative benchmark results showing miss ratio reduction relative to FIFO across multiple cache sizes and trace types; (5) confirmation that implementation integrates cleanly with Cachelib's slab memory management and existing optimizations.

metadata.prompt: To implement S3-FIFO in Cachelib: (1) Use linked lists for S and M queues to support quick demotion and FIFO ordering; (2) Use a hash table for G (ghost) queue to track evicted objects with minimal overhead; (3) Adapt to Cachelib's slab memory pre-allocation and metaprogramming patterns; (4) Implement a trace replay tool that loops through cached traces in closed-loop mode; (5) Focus on cache hit performance and on-demand fill of cache misses using pre-generated object values; (6) Measure miss ratio reduction relative to FIFO baseline to isolate algorithm impact.

skill_drafts.name: Quick Demotion Efficiency Principle
skill_drafts.description: Design principle that rapid demotion of unpopular objects from main cache to secondary storage is critical for cache efficiency. Supported by empirical evidence from TinyLFU's 1% LRU window filtering and S3-FIFO's three-queue design, showing consistent miss ratio improvements across diverse cache workloads.
skill_drafts.objective: Provide evidence-based design guidance for cache eviction algorithm selection and optimization
applicable_signals: Evaluating cache eviction algorithms for efficiency improvements
Explaining performance gaps between FIFO and advanced algorithms
Tuning demotion thresholds or window sizes
contraindications: Write-heavy workloads where demotion cost exceeds benefit
Memory-constrained systems where secondary tier overhead is prohibitive
triggers: Evaluating or designing cache eviction algorithms; explaining why certain algorithms (TinyLFU, S3-FIFO) outperform simpler FIFO; tuning demotion thresholds
constraints: Principle applies primarily to read-heavy and mixed workloads
Effectiveness varies by cache size; TinyLFU shows degradation on small caches (worse than FIFO on ~50% of traces at small sizes)
Requires measurable miss ratio data to validate demotion strategy
cautions: TinyLFU's 1% window does not work uniformly across all traces; P10 point falls below -0.05 on ~20% of traces
Demotion strategy must be tuned per workload type (block, key-value, object)
output_contract: Design decision documented with reference to comparative miss ratio reduction data (vs. FIFO baseline) and demotion mechanism rationale. Caller receives actionable guidance on whether quick demotion is justified for their cache workload and size profile.

examples.input: Designing a cache eviction algorithm for a key-value store with mixed read-write workload
examples.output: Incorporate a quick demotion mechanism (e.g., 1–5% LRU window or multi-queue design) to filter unpopular objects early. Expect 10–32% miss ratio reduction vs. FIFO depending on cache size and workload.
examples.notes: TinyLFU's 1% window is a proven pattern; S3-FIFO's three-queue design is an alternative.

examples.input: Evaluating whether to add demotion overhead to an existing FIFO cache
examples.output: Yes, if cache size is large and workload is read-heavy. Empirical data shows S3-FIFO achieves 14% mean miss ratio reduction on large caches. Avoid if cache is small or write-heavy.
examples.notes: TinyLFU degrades on ~50% of small-cache traces; validate on representative traces first.

metadata.prompt: When evaluating or designing cache eviction algorithms, apply this principle: prioritize mechanisms that quickly demote unpopular objects to secondary tiers. Reference TinyLFU's 1% LRU window filter and S3-FIFO's queue-based demotion as proven patterns. Use miss ratio reduction data (e.g., 32% improvement at P90, 14% mean on large cache sizes) to justify demotion overhead in design trade-offs.
